decisions.reason: As a medium-sized machinery firm with long industrial product cycles, we would keep this core-adjacent unit on the market because the evidence is not clearly negative, though after several years the overlap with other resin systems creates some pruning risk.

We would keep this related resin injection product as a still-viable option, but its similarity to another new unit means it faces a somewhat elevated chance of being rationalized if demand remains only moderate.

We would keep the automatic airless spray gun because it fits the firm’s core coating equipment business and is likely inexpensive to continue offering while niche demand continues to reveal its value.

We would keep the manual airless spray gun for now since catalog carrying costs are likely limited, although a more standard product type is easier to discontinue if sales do not justify attention and inventory.
We would keep the air-assisted airless spray gun because it is close to the established product base and there is no clear signal of failure strong enough to justify abandoning the option.

We would drop the data logger because its downgrade from a dedicated page to a mere mention by 2019 suggests weak traction, and by now the firm has likely learned enough to stop supporting this less proven digital add-on.
